extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/agents, patent owners, and third-party requesters preparing or responding to ex parte reexamination requests before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for preparing and filing a request for ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302-307 and 37 CFR 1.510, including required contents, service, fees, and related submission rules. Targets parties seeking to raise a substantial new question of patentability or patent owners filing requests/amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment and filing date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire fee required under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) for filing a request for reexamination must be paid for the request to be accepted, given a filing date, and published in the Official Gazette. The filing date is the date the request including the entire fee is received, or the date the last portion of the fee is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the entire fee is not paid the request is incomplete (37 CFR 1.510(c),(d)). The requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. If the fee is not paid after opportunity to correct, no determination will be made and the request will ordinarily be placed in the patent file as a prior art citation (see MPEP §2206). If the request is denied or vacated, refund procedures under 37 CFR 1.26(c) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include ‘a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should clearly and in detail set forth what the requester considers the substantial new question(s) of patentability to be in view of prior patents and printed publications, and should show how they are substantially different from questions raised in the prior examination (35 U.S.C. 304; 37 CFR 1.510(b)(1)). If a substantial new question is found as to one claim, all claims will be reexamined (see MPEP §2242).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art limited to patents and printed publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions of patentability must be based on prior art patents or printed publications only; other matters (public use, on sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, 35 U.S.C. 112, fraud, etc.) will not be considered when determining whether to order reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include grounds based on public use, on sale, fraud, or other non-patent/printed-publication matters in the request—such questions will not be considered (MPEP text). A prior art patent or printed publication cannot be used merely as evidence of alleged public use/on sale or insufficiency; it must be applied directly under an appropriate portion of 35 U.S.C. 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of every claim and detailed explanation applying prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must identify every claim for which reexamination is requested and provide a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every such claim (37 CFR 1.510(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere citation of new patents/printed publications without explanation does not comply. The requester must present an explanation of how the cited references are applied to all claims the requester considers to merit reexamination; if filed by the patent owner, the request may also point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions may be based upon the indicated portions of 35 U.S.C. 102 (including subsections (a), (b), (d), (e), (f), (g)) and on 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections derived from those 102 provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §706.02(l)(1) for references qualifying as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103. Double patenting issues may also be proper for consideration in reexamination (e.g., In re Lonardo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited prior art and translations required
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of each patent or printed publication relied on or referred to in the request must be filed with the request (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3)). If documents are not in English, an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts is required; a mere summary or abstract of a non-English document is usually insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full copies of the prior art references so the Office and patent owner can evaluate the application of the references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the patent being reexamined required
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters are required under 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) to include a copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested to serve as the specification for the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full copy of the printed patent (including front page) in double-column format, and include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or prior reexamination certificate; copies of any relevant Federal Court decision, pending complaints, or interference decisions should also be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and serving the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is a person other than the patent owner, the owner must be served with a copy of the request in its entirety to the correspondence address (37 CFR 1.33(c)). A certificate of service must be attached to the request, setting forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy of the request served on the patent owner must include a copy of the certificate of service. Determine the most recent attorney/agent address from the Office register (MPEP §2266.03) and follow service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of requests filed by patent owner including proposed amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may include a proposed amendment with a request under 37 CFR 1.510(e), but any such amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). The determination whether to institute reexamination is made on the claims in effect at the time of the request (without proposed amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner proposes to add claims, excess claim fees (37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4)) may apply. If reexamination is granted, subsequent prosecution will be on the basis of amended claims as presented during the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and declarations related to prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications in more detail may be considered in reexamination (see MPEP §2258).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use affidavits/declarations to clarify dates or contents when appropriate, but ensure they comply with the MPEP guidance for consideration in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: An admission by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication to determine scope/content of prior art in a prior art rejection; an admission per se may not be the basis for a substantial new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions must stand on their own; information supplementing or further defining the admission would be improper. Third parties may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the patent file or court record (those submissions are outside the scope of reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to earlier prosecution and submission of parent application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Include copies of prior art considered during earlier prosecution and copies of parent applications when the content bears on the alleged substantial new question (for example, to establish effective dates or support issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both old and new prior art allows comparison to determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is present (see MPEP §2242). Parent application copies are important when continuation/continuation-in-part timing affects availability of intervening art (see In re Ruscetta, MPEP §201.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reexamination determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination under 35 U.S.C. 303 to order ex parte reexamination is limited to prior art patents and printed publications; if a substantial new question of patentability is raised by such references, an order for ex parte reexamination is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions relating to other grounds (public use, on sale, fraud, etc.) should not be included in the request and will not be considered by the examiner when deciding whether to institute reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of finding a substantial new question on claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a substantial new question of patentability is found as to one claim, all claims of the patent will be reexamined during the ex parte reexamination process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly explain how cited patents/printed publications affect each identified claim since institution for one claim brings all claims into reexamination (see MPEP §2242).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and completeness of submissions (forms and supporting documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters must follow form and content requirements (e.g., include copies of referenced documents, translations, copy of patent, certificate of service, any required forms such as PTO/SB/82, PTO/SB/83 where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete paperwork in the required formats (double-column copy of patent for the proceeding) and include any court decisions, disclaimers, certificates of correction, and other history to present a complete record to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address and representation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the attorney or agent of record per 37 CFR 1.33(c), or if none, to the patent owner at the address of record. Amendments and other papers must be signed by the patent owner or authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change in correspondence address does not withdraw a power of attorney; to have a different attorney receive correspondence, a new power of attorney must be filed. Practitioners have duties (37 CFR 10.23(c)(8)) to notify clients/former clients of Office correspondence that could significantly affect a matter pending before the Office and to timely notify the Office if unable to notify a client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney/agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A request by an attorney or agent of record to withdraw will normally be approved only if at least 30 days remain in any running period for response; withdrawal is effective when approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample form PTO/SB/83 is provided; withdrawal requests should state reasons and provide correspondence address. If less than 30 days remain, requests to withdraw are ordinarily disapproved (see MPEP §402.06).
